domain.name: Database & SQL Operations
domain.description: Relational data modeling, SQL querying, indexing, transactions, migrations, backup/recovery, performance diagnosis, and operational safety for application databases.

competencies.name: Relational Modeling & Constraints
competencies.description: Design tables, keys, relationships, nullability, and constraints to reflect the real domain.
competencies.purpose: Keep application data consistent before relying on application code alone.

units.title: Constraints encode invariant rules
units.content: Primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, not-null rules, and checks make invalid states harder to create.

units.title: Modeling workflow
units.content: Identify entities and stable identifiers; define relationships and cardinality; normalize repeating facts; choose required and optional fields; add constraints; model timestamps and state transitions deliberately; test edge cases.

units.title: Modeling failures
units.content: Avoid comma-separated lists in single columns, using display names as unstable keys, missing uniqueness rules, and modeling every relationship as nullable because it is convenient.

drills.title: Design a project/task schema
drills.prompt: Model projects, tasks, owners, statuses, comments, and audit timestamps.

competencies.name: SQL Querying & Aggregation
competencies.description: Write correct filters, joins, grouping, windowed calculations, and ordered results.
competencies.purpose: Answer operational questions from data reliably.

units.title: Query workflow
units.content: State the question; identify grain of each table; choose joins based on keys; filter before or after aggregation intentionally; group at the required grain; validate counts against known samples; then optimize if needed.

units.title: Query failures
units.content: Avoid accidental many-to-many joins, filtering a left join in WHERE when null-preservation matters, mixing aggregated and nonaggregated fields incorrectly, and assuming row count equals entity count.

units.title: Know the grain before joining
units.content: Most reporting errors come from joining tables whose row meaning was not understood.

drills.title: Debug an inflated revenue query
drills.prompt: Find why joining orders, line items, and payments multiplies totals.

competencies.name: Transactions, Isolation & Concurrency
competencies.description: Use atomic operations, locking concepts, and idempotent patterns for concurrent applications.
competencies.purpose: Prevent partial writes and race-condition data corruption.

units.title: A transaction defines an atomic boundary
units.content: Related writes should either commit together or fail together; concurrency introduces conflicts that must be handled, not assumed away.

units.title: Transactional workflow
units.content: Define invariant; begin transaction; read and update with appropriate constraints or locking strategy; handle conflict or retry conditions; commit only after all required changes succeed; keep transactions short.

units.title: Transaction failures
units.content: Avoid long user-interaction transactions, read-modify-write races without protection, partial multi-table updates, and automatic retries that duplicate non-idempotent side effects.

drills.title: Prevent a double-booking race
drills.prompt: Design a safe transaction for reserving limited capacity under concurrent requests.

competencies.name: Indexes & Query Plans
competencies.description: Use indexes based on access patterns and inspect execution plans before guessing.
competencies.purpose: Improve performance without creating unnecessary write and storage cost.

units.title: Indexes trade read speed for write/storage cost
units.content: Useful indexes support actual filters, joins, and ordering; every index also costs space and maintenance.

units.title: Index tuning workflow
units.content: Capture slow query and parameters; inspect plan; verify row estimates and scan types; identify selective predicates and joins; create or adjust minimal index; compare plan and timing; monitor write impact.

units.title: Index failures
units.content: Avoid indexing every column, creating duplicate indexes, optimizing tiny tables prematurely, and changing indexes without measuring representative queries.

drills.title: Tune a slow filtered query
drills.prompt: Build a plan for a query scanning a large event table by user and date.

competencies.name: Schema Migrations & Data Change
competencies.description: Change schemas safely with backward compatibility, validation, and rollback thinking.
competencies.purpose: Evolve databases without breaking running applications or losing data.

units.title: Migration workflow
units.content: Define old and new schema plus application compatibility; back up or snapshot where appropriate; use additive, backfill, switch, and remove phases for risky changes; test on representative data; monitor; remove old structures only after verification.

units.title: Expand then contract
units.content: For live systems, adding compatible structures before removing old ones reduces deployment coupling.

units.title: Migration failures
units.content: Avoid one-shot destructive column changes, rewriting huge tables during peak load without planning, and deploying code that requires a schema state that is not yet present.

drills.title: Plan a zero-surprise column migration
drills.prompt: Change a frequently used status representation while keeping an app deployable.

competencies.name: Backup, Restore & Recovery
competencies.description: Create backups that can actually restore required data within acceptable loss and time limits.
competencies.purpose: Treat recovery as a tested capability, not a checkbox.

units.title: A backup is unproven until restored
units.content: Successful backup jobs do not guarantee usable recovery; restores must be tested and timing and data-loss expectations defined.

units.title: Recovery workflow
units.content: Define recovery-point and recovery-time needs; choose logical or physical backup strategy; protect backup credentials and encryption; retain multiple generations; perform test restores; document verification and recovery steps.

units.title: Backup failures
units.content: Avoid storing the only backup on the same disk, never testing restore, overwriting all generations with corruption, and assuming snapshots replace application-consistent backups automatically.

drills.title: Design a restore drill
drills.prompt: Plan a monthly restore test for a small application database.

competencies.name: Database Health & Operational Monitoring
competencies.description: Monitor connections, locks, disk, slow queries, replication or backup status, and growth.
competencies.purpose: Detect issues before they become outages.

units.title: Health review
units.content: Check availability and error rate; connection-pool saturation; long transactions and locks; slow-query trends; disk free space; table and index growth; backup freshness; replication lag if applicable; correlate with application changes.

units.title: Operations failures
units.content: Avoid restarting the database before capturing evidence, treating CPU alone as root cause, ignoring disk growth, and increasing connection limits without understanding pool behavior.

units.title: Database incidents often start outside the database
units.content: Application deploys, traffic spikes, network issues, and bad queries can create database symptoms; correlate across layers.

drills.title: Diagnose rising database latency
drills.prompt: Build an evidence checklist for latency after an application release.

competencies.name: Data Integrity, Auditing & Repair Planning
competencies.description: Detect duplicates, orphaned data, impossible states, and drift before attempting repair.
competencies.purpose: Repair data deliberately without hiding the cause.

units.title: Integrity audit
units.content: Define expected invariants; query violations; quantify scope; preserve evidence; identify source process; design idempotent repair; test on copy or small batch; apply with transaction and logging; add constraints or code fix to prevent recurrence.

units.title: Repair failures
units.content: Avoid deleting duplicates before understanding which record is authoritative, mass-updating without backup, and fixing rows without correcting the process that created them.

units.title: Repair and prevention are separate deliverables
units.content: Cleaning current data does not stop the next bad write; close the source failure too.

drills.title: Plan duplicate customer repair
drills.prompt: Design a safe cleanup for duplicate records referenced by orders and messages.
